title: Choosing People for the Work
note: How a ruler learns which tasks the people he has come to trust can do, and employs them in those tasks.

couplets.plain: The one who looks at both the good and the bad, and whose nature is to choose the good, is the one to employ.
couplets.pm: A ruler first gives a man a middling task, between his inner and outer affairs, to learn if he is fit. If the man examines what is and isn’t proper in it and shows a nature that wants only what is proper, he should then be employed in the higher work of the inner affairs. The past tense “chose” shows that a trial has gone before.

links.quote: looks at both the good and the bad

couplets.plain: Let the work go to the one who can widen the sources of income, build up prosperity and look into whatever trouble comes.
couplets.pm: Let the man serve the ruler who can widen the sources of wealth, use that wealth to increase prosperity, and each day look into and remove the troubles that threaten them all. The sources are those named before, with farming, cattle-keeping and trade. The troubles come from the ruler, those who work for him, kin, enemies and thieves.

links.remove: The kingdom is the old English’s. The Tamil names no ruler and speaks only of the one who does the work.

couplets.plain: Place your trust in the one who truly has these four: loving-kindness, understanding, firmness and freedom from craving.
couplets.pm: A ruler can rest his trust on the man who firmly has these four: loving-kindness towards the ruler, knowledge of what will help him, steadiness in doing it, and no craving for the wealth that comes to hand through it. With these, he can leave the work to the man without having to check any of it.

links.reason: Loving-kindness is the first mark asked of an officer.
Understanding is the second thing looked for in a servant.
Firmness of mind is the third requirement.
Its fourth mark is freedom from craving, the Tamil’s அவா.

couplets.plain: Even after you have trusted them in every way, many people change with the nature of the work.
couplets.pm: Even after being tested every way and given a post, many people in the world change through the nature of the work. Few see the pleasures of kingship as a fault and stay as they were, instead of craving them and turning. So give those who seem to have every virtue a middling task first, find them out and remove them.

links.quote: many people change with the nature of the work

couplets.plain: Work is not something to hand to a favourite. It goes only to one who knows how and can endure to the end.
couplets.pm: By its nature a task can’t be given to a man because he has loving-kindness towards you. It goes only to one who knows the means and can bear the pains of the doing and of its obstacles until it is finished. Work is done by knowledge and power, not by loving-kindness.

links.quote: one who knows how and can endure to the end
not something to hand to a favourite

couplets.plain: Look closely at the doer, look closely at the work, match them to the time, and then act.
couplets.pm: First examine the marks of the one who will do it, then the nature of the work, then see how they fit together with the time, and put him to it. That means reasoning that at this time, one with these marks will finish a work of this kind.

links.reason: Look closely at the doer before handing over the work.
Even with the right worker, the work must be matched to the right time.

couplets.plain: Work out that this person can finish this task by this means, then leave it in their hands.
couplets.pm: Examine point by point that this man can finish this work with these means, and when the three fit together, leave the work to him. The means are helpers, wealth and the like. Leaving it means making him the one responsible for it.

links.quote: this person can finish this task by this means

couplets.plain: Once you have found someone right for a task, make that task theirs.
couplets.pm: Once a ruler has examined a man and decided he is fit to do the work, he should raise him to it, giving him the power to finish it himself. Failing to do this also brings ruin.

links.reason: Once someone is found right for a task, it must be made theirs.

couplets.plain: If you misread the closeness of someone devoted to the work, good fortune will leave you.
couplets.pm: A man who always strives at the work behaves like kin, by right of that work. If the ruler listens to those who resent this and thinks otherwise of him, the goddess of fortune leaves the ruler. If he takes the man’s ease for disrespect and turns on him, no one will work with heart any more, and his wealth is lost.

links.reason: திரு, which he reads as the goddess, walks out on such a master.

couplets.plain: Let the ruler look into it every day. If the one who does the work doesn’t go crooked, the world won’t.
couplets.pm: If the man who does the work doesn’t go crooked, the world doesn’t go crooked, so the ruler should examine his work every day. By examining this one thing he has examined the whole world that depends on it. Let him do this quietly, without harming the man’s standing.

links.quote: Let the ruler look into it every day
If the one who does the work doesn’t go crooked, the world won’t
